description:
Problem. When the brief exceeds `brief_max_bytes` (100000) even without the diff, roughly 1500 or more changed files, the plan's brief mode is `oversize` and `selection._skip_reason` skips every reviewer ("skipped: the brief exceeds the size cap even without the diff"). The run ends pending with cause `all-absent`, which `retry.decide_rerun` treats as retryable, so the hourly sweep (`command_sweep`, `retry.due_for_retry`) redispatches the same head with backoff up to `daily_budget` (6) times a day. Under `findings_delivery: review` each run posts another pending review. No reviewer can ever run on that head, so only the owner's stand-in can satisfy the required check.

Required change.
- Record a distinct pending cause for an oversize plan (add it to `retry.PENDING_CAUSES`), so `decide_rerun` refuses same-head retries for it like it does for integrity and unreported causes.
- The pending review for an oversize head says, in plain words, that the change is too large for the oracle and that the owner's stand-in is the way to merge it, or to split the pull request.
- A new push (new diff) still plans normally.

Out of scope. Raising `brief_max_bytes`, splitting briefs, or reviewing oversize PRs some other way.

Guardrails.
- Never weaken the required `oracle-review` check; the stand-in rule is unchanged and only the owner posts it.
- Very-high tier; verify after merge.
- Worktree via `make worktree-create` and `make agent-write-preflight`; identity Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>; explicit staging; no comments or docstrings; `make comment-policy-check`.
- May ship in one PR with oracle-post-guard-reread-retry-20261009, oracle-protocol-test-gaps-20261009 and oracle-marker-patch-map-file-limit-20261009; each item's acceptance must still be met and named in the PR body.

Decision gate. None: the owner-facing behaviour (stand-in or split) is already the documented path for unreviewable PRs.
